The words

Christ is made the sure Foundation,
Christ the Head and Corner-stone,
Chosen of the Lord, and precious,
Binding all the Church in one,
Holy Sion’s help for ever,
And her confidence alone.

All that dedicated city,
Dearly loved of God on high,
In exultant jubilation
Pours perpetual melody,
God the One in Three adoring
In glad hymns eternally.

To this temple, where we call Thee,
Come, O Lord of hosts, to-day;
With Thy wonted loving-kindness
Hear Thy servants, as they pray;
And Thy fullest benediction
Shed within its walls alway.

Here vouchsafe to all Thy servants
What they ask of Thee to gain,
What they gain from Thee for ever
With the Blessed to retain,
And hereafter in Thy glory
Evermore with Thee to reign.

Laud and honour to the Father,
Laud and honour to the Son,
Laud and honour to the Spirit,
Ever Three, and ever One,
Consubstantial, Co-eternal,
While unending ages run.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum G and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on m (B).
  • Count the time. 3/4 means three crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t and the chromatic de. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Mason Neale translated the Latin hymn in 1851; Hymns Ancient and Modern prints these verses as the second part of his translation. The tune WESTMINSTER ABBEY comes from Henry Purcell (1680).

  • Translated (1851): John Mason Neale (1818–1866)
  • Music (1680): Henry Purcell (1659–1695)
  • Music (1842): Ernest Hawkins (died undefined)

Questions about Christ Is Made the Sure Foundation

What is the doh of Christ Is Made the Sure Foundation?

In this version, in G major, doh is G. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Christ Is Made the Sure Foundation start on?

It starts on m (B in G major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

Is Christ Is Made the Sure Foundation in the public domain?

Yes. John Mason Neale died in 1866, Henry Purcell died in 1695, Ernest Hawkins died in undefined; the words were first published in 1851 and the music in 1680. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
